doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Klan and the Ellman incident
summary: The band knew the Klan was around; Dizzy removed Ellman after a white woman kept looking at him.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So you all were real aware -- you were very aware of the activities of the Klan and other groups in all the areas that you were traveling through?

Oh, well, I mean, you know that -- you know that they around there, even if the Klan wasn't, the people that were around, they were like -- listen, we play a dance -- we played a dance and -- and -- and a Caucasian gal was looking at -- at Ellman [phonetic sp.], I mean, she's ­ - I mean, she's -- you know, she had a few drinks, man, and -- and she just kept and Dizzy says, "Ellman, get off. Get off the band and go get on the bus. Get out of -- no, don't start any trouble." You know. Because that's just the way it was. You know? They'd come, you know, oh! And back off. Yeah.
